content.value:
Most autonomous programs are deterministic — they follow a fixed sequence of commands with no awareness of what's happening around them.

If something goes slightly wrong, the robot keeps executing the same plan blindly.

Marrow gives your robot real-time awareness: spatial awareness (where am I?), time awareness (how much time is left?), and tools to configure and debug behavior without redeploying code.

Key features:

Zones — define geometric regions on the field (polygons, circles) and react when the robot enters or exits them.

Prompter — a pre-match configuration screen that lets drivers pick alliance, starting position, and strategy using the gamepad before autonomous starts.

Settings — persistent key-value storage saved to the Control Hub, so values survive robot restarts.

TimerEx — an extended timer with convenience methods for time-based branching in autonomous.

OpModeManager — static access to the active OpMode, telemetry, and hardware map from anywhere — especially useful for debugging subsystems.

Marrow doesn't replace SolversLib — it extends it.

You still use CommandOpMode, SubsystemBase, MotorEx, and the command scheduler.

Marrow adds awareness layers on top: spatial awareness (Zones), time awareness (TimerEx), and runtime configuration (Prompter, Settings).

You'll use Marrow classes inside your existing SolversLib CommandOpModes, not instead of them.
